result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the generic look well by pointing to the stack of common bakery signals. B is stronger on small-size and one-color problems, such as the logo turning to mud on kraft or reversed stock and failing at 32px. B also commits to one concrete direction rooted in the name: an ampersand drawn as a scored loaf. A offers a menu of options, including type, palette and mark ideas, and keeps little beyond the brown. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers trace the generic look to the same stacked category clichés. A goes further on small-size and one-color failures: avatar size, kraft or dark stock, foil, and the 32px test. A also commits to one concrete idea drawn from the name, an ampersand drawn as a scored loaf, and keeps more of the existing logo. B lists several options without choosing one, rejects more (script, pink, cream), and reads as a longer list of equal items.
